title: Integer Representation
body:
[[Integer]] values are stored as binary

[[Base Conversion]]
[[Complements]] 

Unsigned is the plain reading: every bit has place value $2^i$, so $n$ bits cover
$0$ to $2^n - 1$. Signed uses two's [[Complements|complement]], which makes the top bit
worth $-2^{n-1}$ and gives the range $-2^{n-1}$ to $2^{n-1}-1$.

Nothing in memory records which of the two you meant. The bits `%1111_1111` are 255 or −1
depending entirely on the instruction you use to read them, which is why the 68000 has both
`bcc`/`bcs` (unsigned comparison, carry) and `bge`/`blt` (signed comparison, overflow and
negative). Picking the wrong branch is a classic bug: see [[Status Bits]].

| 68000 size | Suffix | Unsigned | Signed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Byte | `.b` | 0 … 255 | −128 … 127 |
| Word | `.w` | 0 … 65535 | −32768 … 32767 |
| Longword | `.l` | 0 … 4294967295 | −2147483648 … 2147483647 |

Widening a signed value needs `ext`, which copies the sign bit leftwards, not a zero pad.
Narrowing just drops the high bits and silently wraps, which is what a C
[[Type casting|cast]] to a smaller type does too.

An $n$-bit register is doing [[Modular Arithmetic]] in $\mathbb{Z}_{2^n}$, which is the algebraic
reading [[ABSTRACT ALGEBRA]] (MATH 2101) gives all of this. Unsigned overflow is not a fault, it is
reduction mod $2^n$ working exactly as specified, and two's complement is the statement that $-x$
and $2^n - x$ name the same congruence class. Wraparound is the group cycling.
